data.description:
# S6 — Clear the parity bar for Bedrock before it becomes a first-class provider

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/parity.py` defines rebar's non-inferiority bar — structured-output validity, per-criterion
verdict agreement with zero decision-level gold flips, recall and false-accept within 2pp, and error rate — and
it was required before the last LLM substrate swap (the LangGraph → pydantic-ai cutover). Routing gate traffic
through Bedrock is a substrate change of the same kind: different API surface (Converse), different capability
flags, and a different structured-output path. Declaring Bedrock "first-class" without running that bar would
make the tier label unearned.

## Approach

Run the existing `parity_report` machinery with the standing eval corpus, v1 = direct Anthropic and
v2 = Bedrock-hosted Claude [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550], same model family and decoding params, N≥3 repeats — the
protocol `parity.py` already documents. No new gate logic is written; this story supplies the corpus run and
records the report. It runs as an env-gated live job modeled on the existing weekly live-LLM jobs, not as a
blocking CI job, because it needs funded model calls.

The report is the deliverable and it is **decision-bearing**: if Bedrock fails any criterion, this ticket
records the failure and the epic's first-class claim for Bedrock is revisited before the bot cutover
proceeds — rather than shipping a tier label the evidence does not support.

**Alternative rejected:** asserting parity from the fact that it is the same underlying model. The Converse API
differs in structured-output handling and cache semantics, which is precisely what criterion (a) measures.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — no logic change expected; wiring only if the driver needs a provider parameter.
- `.github/workflows/` — the env-gated live parity job.
- This ticket's comments — the recorded `ParityReport`.

## Testing

LLM-surface eval tier (§10): pinned model and decoding settings, paired runs differing only in provider,
multiple samples against the predeclared thresholds already encoded in `parity_report`, scored deterministically
by the existing report function.

- the offline gate logic stays exercised by the existing synthetic-record unit tests (no regression).
- the live run reports both rates, not just the pass/fail bit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a `ParityReport` comparing Bedrock to direct Anthropic on the standing corpus (N≥3 repeats) is attached as
      a comment on this ticket, including validity, agreement, recall, false-accept, and error rate
- [ ] the report states pass or fail against each `parity.py` criterion explicitly
- [ ] if any criterion fails, a comment records the decision taken (remediate, or drop Bedrock's first-class
      claim) and the epic is updated to match
- [ ] the live job is env-gated and does not run in default CI (`make test` unaffected)
data.title: S6 — clear the parity bar for Bedrock before it becomes a first-class provider
